c74object.name: evi_trig
c74object.digest: A GenExpr file, part of 'evieve', for using via 'require()'
c74object.description:
evi_trig.genexpr is a .genexpr file and is part of the 'evieve' Package.
It is for using in a gen.codebox~ or in another .genexpr file via the require() command.
By declaring require("evi_trig.genexpr"); at the top of a codebox you can then access all of the functions included in this file.
About this File:
Some trigonomic approximations: cos, sin, tan, arctan, © 2001 The Ganssle Group. Approximations are faster than library functions but less accurate. You should be careful using approximations - they can break your code. In evieve all approximations are tested to work on the code in which they are used. Note, in this 'evi_trig' GenExpr code, in terms of cos/sin CPU savings, only '73' or lower are worthwhile, for 121 or higher there is no point over library cos/sin. See the source code for more (commented out) code if you are interested.

entry.name: makeCosPhase ( )
entry.description:
Make phase and quadrant for all of the cos/sin approximations
In 1: type=input: x, Phase 0..TWOPI
Return 1: Phase, Phase for cos/sin approximations
Return 2: Quadrant, The quadrant to switch to for the cos/sin approximations

entry.name: cosQ32 ( )
entry.description:
Polynomial computes cosine(x) accurate to about 3.2 decimal digits over the range [0, PI/2]
In 1: type=input: x, The input argument is in radians
Return 1: Cos, One quadrant of cosine()

entry.name: cos32 ( )
entry.description:
Reduces the input argument's range to [0, PI/2], then calls the approximator
In 1: type=input: x, Phase 0..TWOPI
Return 1: Cos, Approximate cos() of input

entry.name: sin32 ( )
entry.description:
The sine is just cosine shifted by HALFPI, calls the cosine approximation
In 1: type=input: x, Phase 0..TWOPI
Return 1: Sin, Approximate sin() of input

entry.name: cos32param ( )
entry.description:
Param rate version of 'cos32()' (keep out of while loop in export)
In 1: type=input: x, Phase 0..TWOPI
Return 1: Cos, Approximate cos() of input

entry.description:
